title: Low-Code and No-Code
seoTitle: Low-Code and No-Code Explained for Business Owners
seoDescription: Low-code and no-code tools let you build apps and automations with little programming. What they suit, where they break, costs and when custom code wins.
summary: Low-code and no-code platforms let people build apps, forms and automations mostly by configuring screens and drag-and-drop steps instead of writing code. They are fast for simple, low-risk workflows; custom code becomes the better choice as logic, volume, security needs or user numbers grow.

dataPoints.label: Examples
dataPoints.value: Zapier, Make, n8n (automation); Zoho Creator, Microsoft Power Apps, Glide (apps)

dataPoints.label: Good for
dataPoints.value: Internal forms, simple approvals, notifications, prototypes

dataPoints.label: Limits
dataPoints.value: Complex rules, high volume, testing, version control, per-user or per-task pricing

dataPoints.label: Hidden risk
dataPoints.value: Critical processes built by one person that nobody else understands

body:
## When to choose low-code

- The workflow is simple and not business-critical.
- A non-developer will maintain it.
- You need something working this week.

## When to move to custom code

- Failures would lose orders or money.
- Costs grow with every task or user.
- You need proper testing, audit trails and security.

See [workflow automation with n8n, Make or custom code](/blog/workflow-automation-with-n8n-make-or-custom-code-how-to-choose).

faqs.a: Its source is available to self-host under its licence terms, with a paid cloud version. Hosting and maintenance still cost time and money.

faqs.q: Can a low-code app grow into a full product?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but many teams rebuild in custom code once usage grows, so keep business rules documented.
